newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan shipping talks continue, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan shipping talks continue, U.S. says.

text.p: The U.S. Maritime Administration said Thursday that talks with Japan aimed at ending a dispute over port practices in Japan were continuing.

U.S. and Japan transportation officials have held two days of talks this week in an effort to end the dispute before April 14, when the United States is set to slap a $100,000 per vessel surcharge against Japanese ships.
"The discussions are continuing, but the Maritime Administration will have no statement this evening," an agency spokesman said.
The Federal Maritime Commission voted to impose the surcharge on Japanese ships in retaliation for what it said were unfair, restrictive practices at Japanese ports.

The FMC said the Japan Harbor Transportation Association (JHTA), which is made up of port cargo-handling firms and which mediates between labor unions and shipping companies, has put in place costly and restrictive practices that discriminate against foreign vessels.
Japan has urged the United States to withdraw the sanctions and port workers in Japan have staged protests in opposition to the U.S. move.
